## Bio

I am a physics PhD student at the **University of Massachusetts Amherst**, working with Prof. Benjamin Heidenreich at the Amherst Center for Fundamental Interactions. My research develops theoretical and computational tools to understand strongly coupled quantum field theories, drawing on string theory, conformal field theory, tensor networks, and Monte Carlo methods.

I work across three areas: high-energy theory (geometric engineering, superconformal field theories, S-duality, brane constructions), condensed matter theory (boundary RG flows, superfluidity, symmetry-enriched criticality), and computational physics (DMRG, worm and cluster algorithms, and emerging connections to machine learning). A unifying thread is the use of string-theoretic and conformal-field-theoretic structures --- generalized symmetries, dualities, and categorical data --- to illuminate physics in both domains.

Before UMass, I studied impurity dynamics in Dirac fermion systems during my master's thesis at IISER Bhopal, which resulted in a published paper in condensed matter theory.

## Research Interests

- **High-Energy Theory**
  - Lagrangian descriptions of non-Lagrangian $\mathcal{N}=2$ SCFTs via geometric engineering and brane tilings
  - $\mathcal{N}=1$ flavor orientifolds: discrete torsion, Wilson lines, and S-duality
  - Quad-CFTs and infrared phases of 4d $\mathcal{N}=1$ theories with tensor matter
  - Mirror symmetry aspects of quad-CFTs (type IIA with D6/O6-branes)
  - Discrete symmetries, orbifolding, and gauging in 2D CFTs; connections to the swampland

- **Condensed Matter & Many-Body Theory**
  - Impurity dynamics in Dirac fermion systems
  - Boundary RG flow and symmetry-enriched criticality in interacting Majorana chains
  - DMRG, MPS, and tensor-network approaches for extracting conformal data
  - Superfluid transition in 3D Bose gases with long-range Coulomb interactions
  - Monte Carlo studies of classical and quantum many-body systems

- **Computational & Numerical Methods, ML Directions**
  - Long-range worm and cluster Monte Carlo algorithms
  - Tensor-network computations and analysis pipelines
  - Physics-informed generative models (diffusion models, normalizing flows for sampling)
  - Tensor cross-interpolation for high-dimensional function approximation
  - Early-stage work on measurement-induced phase transitions

- **Future Directions**
  - Generalized symmetries (higher-form, non-invertible, categorical) as a bridge between string-theoretic SCFTs and lattice models of quantum matter

For a detailed overview, see the [Research](research.qmd) page or browse the [Notes & Expositions](notes/index.qmd).
